key_claims.claim: Neonatal hypoglycemia below 40 mg/dL in late preterm infants is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes at age six or older.
Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are associated with a greater than three-fold increased risk of diabetic retinopathy and other ophthalmic disease in long-term follow-up.
Vaginal progesterone and cerclage may act through complementary rather than redundant pathways for preterm birth prevention in women with short cervix.
Second-stage cesarean is the strongest risk factor for unintentional hysterotomy extension, which is linked to subsequent preterm birth.
Cardiovascular maladaptation during HDP may persist postpartum and mechanistically link abnormal pregnancy hemodynamics to long-term CVD risk.
